newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ING sees South Africa 2.4 pct GDP growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: ING sees South Africa 2.4 pct GDP growth in '97.

text.p: Stockbroking firm ING Barings on Tuesday forecast GDP growth for South Africa of 2.4 percent in 1997, but only if a recent rate hike is reversed by the second quarter of the year.

If the rate rise remained, growth could come in at less that two percent, mainly as a result of the squeeze on consumption expenditure and investment due to the hike, ING economist Hania Farhan said in an economic review.

"On the supply side, the strong agricultural season of 1996 came off a very low base in 1995 -- a situation which will be reversed in 1997, where agricultural growth will come off a very high base," Farhan added.
The growth estimates were based on assumptions that the Bank rate would drop by three percent by the end of 1998 to 14 percent -- 1.5 percent of which was expected in 1997.
South Africa's Bank rate was last hiked on November 21 to 17.00 percent from 16 percent.

The estimates were also based on assumptions of real wage growth of around one percent in 1996 and around 0.5 percent in 1997, a gradual approach to the removal of exchange controls, a total rand depreciation of around ten percent in 1997 and around eight percent in 1998 and that European growth would pick up in 1997 and be maintained in 1998.
Farhan said 1998 should see a rebound in growth to around 3.5 percent if the expected three percent rate cut materialised by the end of that year.
She emphasised the importance of raising the savings and investment ratios to levels above 20 percent of GDP by 1998 at the latest.
"Otherwise, we do not believe that government targets of sustainable five to six percent growth rates by 1999/2000 are achievable," Farhan said.
